title: Why one database hits a wall — and how sharding gets you past it
credit: Spec piece · Concept, animation & edit by MAEKEN · Not affiliated with or endorsed by PlanetScale

lines.text: Every app starts with one database.
Traffic doubles. Then it doubles again.
Your p99 latency — the slowest one percent of requests — starts to climb.
And that's the part your users feel.
The first fix is a bigger machine.
It works — until there's no bigger machine to buy.
Sharding cuts one huge table into smaller pieces, each on its own server.
A routing layer reads a key, like the user ID, and sends each query to the one shard that owns it.
Now every server carries only a slice of the load.
Need more room? Add another shard.
Capacity grows sideways, instead of hitting a ceiling.
The hard part is doing it live: moving data between shards while traffic keeps flowing.
That's exactly what systems like Vitess were built for.
lines.say: That's exactly what systems like Vi-tess were built for.
